citeAs: Chen, C., Liu, M., Codella, N., Li, Y., Yuan, L., and Gurari, D. (2024). Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities. arXiv:2311.15562.
creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, Danna Gurari (University of Texas at Austin, Microsoft, University of Colorado Boulder)
description: VQAonline is the first Visual Question Answering dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case. Sourced from online question answering community forums (Stack Exchange), it contains 64,696 VQAs with authentic natural language questions, images, context, and answers validated by the individuals who asked the questions. It spans 105 diverse topics across five super-categories, with answers averaging 173 words in length.
name: VQAonline
publisher: University of Texas at Austin; Microsoft
rai:annotationsPerItem: For user intention annotations: 2 independent crowdworker annotations per VQA, with a third annotator used as a tiebreaker when the first two disagreed (resulting in a majority vote label from 3 annotations). For domain expert evaluation: 6 model-generated answers rated per VQA by one domain expert.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers for user intention annotation: located in the United States, had completed more than 500 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) with over a 95% approval rating. Domain experts for human evaluation: ten individuals each with at least a Master's degree in a field related to their assigned VQA topic (Physical Fitness, Botany, Music, Mechanics, Politics, Law, Chinese Language, Economics, Statistics, and Artificial Intelligence); required to be located in the United States to guarantee English proficiency.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For user intention taxonomy development: four rounds of annotation analysis on 105 visual questions by two annotators (authors). Agreement accuracy improved from 53.3% to 87.5% and Cohen's kappa improved from 45.24% to 84.69% across rounds. For final user intention annotations: 25 out of 105 VQAs had disagreements between the two crowdworkers, requiring a third annotator to break the tie.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (for user intention annotations); custom home-grown web-based interface (for domain expert human evaluation)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For user intention annotations: crowdworkers were provided instructions, taxonomy definitions, and two examples per user intention category. Each worker received one-on-one Zoom training and passed a qualifying annotation test. Workers were shown the question, context, and answer for each VQA and asked to assign one primary intent category. For domain expert human evaluation: ten domain experts (each with at least a Master's degree in a relevant field) were each assigned 20 VQAs on their topic and asked to rate six model-generated answers per VQA as incorrect (0), partially correct (0.5), or correct (1).
rai:dataBiases: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and the Internet. The geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more users from countries like the US, India, and Europe and fewer from countries like Egypt. Most visual questions are written in English, which may bias toward English-speaking users.
rai:dataCollection: Data was scraped from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange, using publicly-available data spanning from August 2010 to November 2022. All examples containing four components were collected: a natural language question (post "title"), a natural language context (post "body"), an image (URL link), and at least one answer. Only examples where the question poster marked an "accepted answer" were retained.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data was sourced from the Stack Exchange archive hosted at https://archive.org/details/stackexchange in XML format. The initial candidate pool contained 330,705 visual questions before filtering.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas. Geographic representation is unbalanced (more from US, India, Europe; less from countries like Egypt). The dataset is constrained to Stack Exchange users who have access to mobile devices and the Internet. Some topics have very few examples (as few as 10). The dataset contains multilingual VQAs but is predominantly English. Models trained on Stack Exchange data may have seen VQAonline data, creating potential data contamination issues for benchmarking.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Starting from 330,705 candidate visual questions: (1) removed visual questions without an accepted answer (leaving 165,766); (2) removed visual questions with scores of 0 or less for either the question or answer (leaving 119,177); (3) removed visual questions with multiple images or GIFs (leaving 85,573); (4) removed visual questions with visual answers (leaving 65,849); (5) removed examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided URL link (leaving 64,696 final examples). All images were converted to PNG format for data format consistency. Additionally, 75 technology topics (e.g., Stack Overflow, LaTeX) were excluded because they typically involve language/code problems.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to facilitate research community progress on VQA models for authentic use cases. Improved models could benefit real-world applications including other community question answering platforms (e.g., Yahoo! Answers, Wiki Answers, Quora), learning assistance VQA tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, as well as visual search and browsing. The dataset also facilitates exploration of the hallucination issue in authentic use cases.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking VQA models on authentic use cases; evaluating long-form answer generation; few-shot learning (with provided train/validation/test splits); research on multilingual VQA; research on text recognition in images; research on hallucination in vision-language models; improving evaluation metrics for lengthy textual answers.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5 was used via zero-shot prompting to bootstrap the initial user intention taxonomy categories. DeepSolo (state-of-the-art text spotter model) was used to detect text presence in all images in the dataset (finding 76% of images contain text).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset is sourced from publicly posted content on Stack Exchange. No explicit collection of personal or sensitive information is described, though user-generated content from Stack Exchange users is included.

null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper describes filtering steps (e.g., removing examples where images could not be downloaded) as preprocessing, not as handling of missing data in the traditional sense. No explicit discussion of missing data handling beyond image download failures is present.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation, augmentation, or resampling of the dataset itself is described.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
